title: Annotated routing heuristics — engineering journal
summary: Working notes exploring a compact, score-driven routing policy that blends latency SLOs, per-request cost budgets, and regional reliability signals. Includes an annotated decision tree, rollout ideas, and experiment sketches.
body:
Purpose and context:
- Quick working journal for policy experiments: we need a simple-to-reason-about routing heuristic that ops can inspect, that the control plane can evaluate cheaply, and that behaves predictably across regions when capacity fluctuates.
- Focus: per-request routing decision (choose: local-hosted, regional-dedicated, fallback-remote, degraded-quantized) using three signals: latency estimate, cost delta, reliability/confidence.

Requirements / constraints (practical):
- Decision path must be computable in <1ms in the control plane (no expensive ML scoring during request-time).
- Supports soft-SLOs: three levels (strict, normal, best-effort) mapped from customer tier.
- Must allow deterministic simulation reproducible from recorded traces.
- Rollout-friendly: can toggle each branch to on/off, and can A/B by request-group.

Signals we actually have and their noise characteristics:
- p95-rt(region, model, seq): median-stable, sampled at 1m; 99th more volatile.
- cost-per-token(model, flavor): deterministic from pricing table + estimated tokens.
- infra-healthy(region): boolean-like but derived from aggregated recent errors (drop if error_rate > 0.5%).
- instance-warmth / kv-cache-hit: || reduces effective latency by ~10-40ms.
- capacity-headroom(region): continuous 0..1 from alloc-utilization model.

Scoring approach (compact, interpretable):
- Compute three scaled scores in [0..1]:
  S_latency = clamp(1 - (est_latency / slo_target), 0, 1)  // higher is better
  S_cost = clamp(1 - ((cost_delta / cost_budget)), 0, 1)   // cost_delta = candidate_cost - cheapest_candidate_cost
  S_reliability = infra_health_score (0..1) derived from error/latency anomalies
- Aggregate via weighted sum: Score = wL * S_latency + wC * S_cost + wR * S_reliability
- Weights (example starting point): strict-tier => [0.6, 0.1, 0.3]; normal => [0.5, 0.25, 0.25]; best-effort => [0.3, 0.5, 0.2]
- Thresholds decide branch selection. Keep thresholds coarse to be interpretable.

Annotated decision tree (ASCII, annotated with intent):
- Root: compute candidate list = {local-hosted, regional-dedicated, remote-fallback, quantized-degraded}
- For each candidate compute Score (as above) and also compute worst_case_latency_estimate and cost_delta

Decision heuristic (first-cut):
                             [start]
                                |
               compute Scores for each candidate
                                |
                   pick candidate with highest Score
                                |
            if chosen.Score >= T_accept -> ROUTE to chosen
            else -> check fallback rules (below)

Fallback rules (illustrative):
- If top Score < T_accept but top.S_reliability < R_min -> prefer any candidate with S_reliability >= R_min even if cost higher (safety over cost).
- If top.Score < T_accept and (top.worst_case_latency > slo_target * 1.5) -> route to remote-fallback if its S_latency >= 0.6 (willing to pay latency for reliability/cost tradeoff).
- If capacity-headroom(local) < 0.2 -> degrade to quantized-degraded only for best-effort tier; for strict/normal fallback to regional-dedicated.

Example thresholds (start point — conservative):
- T_accept = 0.65 (accept route without extra checks)
- R_min = 0.7 (minimal infra health)
- cost_budget: per-request % above cheapest allowed (e.g., 30% for normal, 10% strict, 80% best-effort)

Why this is different from pure LCR (latency-cost-reliability):
- We compute a normalized composite score so policy decisions remain single-dimensional (easier to reason about) but maintain separate fallback checks for pathological cases (avoid letting a high score hide bad tail-risk on reliability).
- We intentionally bias weights by customer tier to make economic tradeoffs explicit.

Control plane integration notes:
- Evaluate scores in the control plane's policy-eval module; cache last-minute candidate metadata (latency_est, cost_est, infra_health) in a short-lived store (TTL=10s) to avoid recompute overhead.
- Expose feature flags to flip on/off any candidate (e.g., emergency-disable-quantized) and a global override to prefer cheapest for cost-accounting experiments.
- Log the chosen_score and reason_code for every routed request (reason_code enums: TOP_SCORE_ACCEPT, FALLBACK_HEALTH, FALLBACK_CAPACITY, DEGRADATION_QUANTIZED, OVERRIDE) — useful for retrospective evals.

Simulation and evaluation plan (small experiments):
- Offline: replay 7 days of traces via policy-sim harness, compute per-req chosen branch, then aggregate: p50/p95 latency, cost, error-rate by route and tier.
- Hypothesis A: Weighted-sum scoring reduces tail-latency regressions vs cost-only heuristics for normal tier.
- Hypothesis B: Introducing the reliability-min fallback reduces customer-visible spikes during infra health dips with modest cost increase.
- Metric targets: <2% increase in overall cost for a 20% reduction in p99 tail failures for normal tier.

Rollout plan (practical):
- Canary: 1% traffic for 48h, collect logs, ensure reason_code distribution looks sane.
- Ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 100% by application slice with kill-switch.
- Observability: add quick dashboards: route distribution, reason_code frequency, scoring histogram, per-tier cost delta.

Operational play snippets (notes to self):
- DO: Keep T_accept a feature flag per-deploy so we can nudge conservatism during incidents.
- DO: Add a short-circuit that if infra_health suddenly drops in a region by >0.2 in 30s, mark region emergency and immediately divert new requests to pre-configured remotes.
- DON'T: Mix ML model scoring at request-time unless it's a background scorer with cached outputs. We want determinism.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to best estimate worst_case_latency (we currently have p99 which is noisy). Maybe use EWMA on p95 and add fudge factor rather than raw p99. TODO: experiment.
- Should we encode customer budget as absolute token-cost or relative cost-delta? Current lean is relative % because cheapest model for short prompts can be different.
- Can isolation zones (for compliance) override Score weights? Yes, need policy metadata to force min S_reliability thresholds for those customers.
- Evaluate adding a simple continuous penalty if a candidate has had "recent-failures" in last N minutes — this will help avoid flipping flakily between nodes.

Appendix — quick pseudocode:
function route_request(req, tier, candidates):
  for c in candidates:
    c.S_latency = clamp(1 - (est_latency(c)/slo_target(tier)), 0, 1)
    c.S_cost = clamp(1 - (cost_delta(c)/cost_budget(tier)), 0, 1)
    c.S_reliability = infra_score(c.region)
    c.score = wL(tier)*c.S_latency + wC(tier)*c.S_cost + wR(tier)*c.S_reliability
  best = argmax(candidates, by=score)
  if best.score >= T_accept(tier): return route(best, reason="TOP_SCORE_ACCEPT")
  // fallback health-first
  if best.S_reliability < R_min:
    alt = pick_any_with(candidates, S_reliability >= R_min, prefer=score)
    if alt: return route(alt, reason="FALLBACK_HEALTH")
  if best.worst_case_latency > slo_target(tier)*1.5:
    alt = candidate with S_latency>=0.6 and highest score
    if alt: return route(alt, reason="FALLBACK_LATENCY")
  // capacity degrade path
  if capacity_headroom(best.region) < 0.2 and tier != 'best-effort':
    alt = regional-dedicated if available else remote-fallback
    return route(alt, reason="FALLBACK_CAPACITY")
  // else go with best and log degraded_reason
  return route(best, reason="TOP_SCORE_ACCEPT_POSTCHECKS")

Notes on multi-region specifics:
- Prefer local routing when S_latency is high and S_reliability close to regional leader within 5% to avoid unnecessary cross-region cost.
- For geo-sensitive customers, attach policy tag: "geo_strict" which forces local-first and forces cost_budget to large number to avoid cross-region.
- Consider adding a routing-penalty for cross-region egress cost in S_cost calculation so aggregated cost math is accurate.

Final pendings (short list):
- Write sim harness config and baseline scenarios (normal-traffic, incident-spike, regional-evacuation).
- Flesh out reason_code enums in policy-eval proto.
- Add quick alert thresholds tied to reason_code spikeyness (e.g., sudden rise in FALLBACK_HEALTH).

End of notes — these are rough, please critique. If we like the composite-score + fallback checks pattern we can formalize into a policy DSL snippet for the control plane.

Quick sign-off line: Jordan — jotting initial heuristics before turning into a formal policy PR.
